newsitem.title: CHINA: China farm bank loans to rise 10.5 bln yuan in '97.
newsitem.headline: China farm bank loans to rise 10.5 bln yuan in '97.

text.p: The Agriculture Bank of China plans to extend 54 billion yuan ($6.5 billion) in loans to agriculture in 1997, up 10.5 billion yuan from last year, the Financial Times said on Monday.
These loans would be used to build water conservancy projects and overall agricultural development, the newspaper quoted bank vice president He Linxiang as saying.

The bank's profits also rose strongly, increasing to 518 billion yuan in 1996 from about 70 million yuan in 1995, the newspaper said. It did not specify whether the figures were before tax. Chinese institutions usually give pre-tax profits.
Bank deposits rose to 894.3 billion yuan in 1996, up 28.9 percent from 1995, the China Business Times said.
The Agriculture Bank, one of China's four main state-owned banks, also extended 776.9 billion yuan in loans in 1996, up 18.4 percent from last year, it said but gave no more details.
